title: Coordinate-divisor criterion for purity of a monomial trait model
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a Noetherian local domain of dimension one and principal maximal ideal; a uniformizer $\pi$ generates that maximal ideal. Let $\ell$ be invertible in $R$, let $n\geq1$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbf N$ be not all zero. Put
$$V=\operatorname{Spec}R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(\prod_iT_i^{a_i}-\pi).$$
Suppose $V$ is regular. For $a_i>0$ let $h_i:H_i\hookrightarrow V$ be the regular effective Cartier divisor cut out by $T_i=0$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; effective Cartier means locally defined by a nonzerodivisor. Then $V$ is punctually pure if and only if every supported Kummer map
$$A_{H_i}\longrightarrow h_i^!A_V(1)[2]$$
is an isomorphism. No condition is imposed for indices with $a_i=0$.

source.place: Expose XVI Lemma 3.5.13(iv), printed p.251; Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2.

proof.text: Put $B=R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(\prod_jT_j^{a_j}-\pi)$ and $k=R/(\pi)$. For $a_i>0$, imposing $T_i=0$ makes the monomial zero, so the two quotient maps fixing the remaining variables give $B/(T_i)\simeq k[T_j:j\ne i]$. Thus $H_i$ is affine $(n-1)$-space over $k$. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$, the relation gives $\pi\in\mathfrak q$ if and only if $T_i\in\mathfrak q$ for some $a_i>0$: a prime contains a finite product exactly when it contains a factor, and a zero exponent contributes the unit $1$. Hence the underlying special fibre is exactly $\bigcup_{a_i>0}|H_i|$. This is a set-theoretic covering; no reducedness of the special fibre is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(iv), proof, printed p.251: coordinate divisors are affine spaces and cover the special fibre.

proof.text: The ring $k$ is a field because $(\pi)$ is the maximal ideal of $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $k[T_j:j\ne i]$ is Noetherian and regular, including when there are no remaining variables. Thus each $H_i$ is a regular Noetherian scheme. The inverse of $\ell$ in $R$ maps to an inverse in $k$, in this polynomial ring and in each of its localizations. A field contains its prime field $k_0$, which is $\mathbf Q$ or $\mathbf F_p$ (with $p\ne\ell$, since $\ell$ is invertible). Let $h\in H_i$. The local ring $\mathcal O_{H_i,h}$ is a Noetherian regular local $k_0$-algebra with $\ell$ invertible, of dimension $d_h$. Apply [lem-per-trait-test-prime-field-local-input] to it: the canonical Kummer map $A_{\kappa(h)}\to j_h^!A(d_h)[2d_h]$ for its closed point is an isomorphism. This is exactly the map of [def-per-punctual-purity] at $h$, built from the same class of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] and the same closed-support adjunction. Hence every $H_i$ is punctually pure.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(iv), proof, printed p.251; Proposition 3.2.5, printed p.245. Polynomial regularity: Stacks Tag 00OQ, algebra.tex, proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring.

proof.text: Let $U=D(\pi)\subset V$. The localization $R[1/\pi]$ is a field: primes of this localization correspond to primes of $R$ avoiding $\pi$; the only such prime is $(0)$, since any nonzero prime strictly below the maximal ideal would give a chain of length two in the one-dimensional local domain. A domain whose only prime is zero is a field, since every proper principal ideal is contained in a maximal ideal. Thus $U$ is a scheme over the field $R[1/\pi]$, hence over its prime field. Its local rings are those of the assumed regular scheme $V$, and its coordinate ring is the Noetherian localization $B[1/\pi]$. Let $u\in U$. Then $\mathcal O_{U,u}=\mathcal O_{V,u}$ is a Noetherian regular local algebra over the prime field of $R[1/\pi]$, with $\ell$ invertible. Apply [lem-per-trait-test-prime-field-local-input] to it: the canonical closed-point Kummer map is an isomorphism. Since $U_u$ and $V_u$ are identical, with the same residue field, dimension, and closed-point Kummer map of [def-per-punctual-purity], $V$ is punctually pure at every point of $U$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(iv), proof, printed p.251: punctual purity of the generic fibre; Proposition 3.2.5, printed p.245; Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, printed p.244.

proof.text: Assume $V$ is punctually pure. For each $a_i>0$, apply [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three] to $h_i:H_i\hookrightarrow V$. Both schemes are regular Noetherian, $\ell$ is invertible, and this is the regular effective Cartier divisor in the statement, of codimension one. Condition (b) is Step 2 and condition (c) follows from the assumption on $V$. The implication (b),(c)$\Rightarrow$(a) gives precisely $A_{H_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}h_i^!A_V(1)[2]$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(iv), printed p.251, only-if direction via Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244.

proof.text: Conversely assume the displayed Kummer map is an isomorphism for every $a_i>0$. For each such $i$, conditions (a) and (b) of [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three] hold by assumption and Step 2; its hypotheses are the same as in Step 4. It yields condition (c), punctual purity of $V$ at every point of $H_i$. Step 1 covers all points where $\pi$ vanishes by these divisors, while Step 3 covers the complementary open $D(\pi)$. Every point of $V$ is therefore punctually pure. Zero exponents add no factor to this covering and require no divisor-purity hypothesis.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(iv), proof, printed p.251, if direction via Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244.
